We've seen numerous reports about Apple Vision Pro applications in medical settings. This week, Stryker announced the completion of the first surgical procedure using an innovative application on Vision Pro.

The procedure was a hip arthroscopy, utilizing the SportSuite Vision application, which brings "critical digital content into the surgeon's virtual space." Content includes arthroscopic imagery, HipCheck, HipMap, and CT scan images.

Below is Stryker's description of the application:

SportSuite Vision brings critical digital content into the surgeon's visual space, allowing them to simultaneously view physical objects and digital tools in the operating room, such as arthroscopic imagery, HipCheck, HipMap, and CT scan images. During arthroscopic procedures, surgeons typically rely on multiple displays placed throughout the operating room to access imaging and surgical data. By integrating multiple data sources into the surgeon's field of view, this technology can reduce reliance on traditional displays and support a smoother, more ergonomic surgical workflow.

SportSuite Vision received FDA De Novo authorization on July 17. Stryker stated that this is the first FDA-authorized application approved for use with Vision Pro during surgery.
